Subject: Support coverage slab structuring & volume incentive

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo today. BrightCart is close to a decision but procurement and SRE have a couple of asks before we move forward. Can you send a concise breakdown of how Redwood structures: 

- Uptime tiers (what exactly is covered at 99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95)
- Per-incident / month credit calculations and how credits scale with higher commit levels
- Response time SLAs (P1/P2/P3 definitions) and escalation coverage (on-call handoffs, exec escalation)
- Whether business-hours vs 24x7 response can be differentiated in pricing

We also need an example for a $300k annual commit that shows the effective unit price after volume incentives and any credit/uptime uplift. Procurement would prefer a short spreadsheet + a one-page summary.

I attached a list of specific questions the SRE team had. Can we aim to get something by EOD Tuesday our time? If useful, loop in whomever handles pricing and ops.

Thanks,
Tom Riley
Head of Procurement — BrightCart
tom.riley@brightcart.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-13T10:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Support coverage slab structuring & volume incentive

Tom —

Appreciate the clear list. Looping in Jordan (deal lead) and Kimberly (pricing/ops) to pull together the spreadsheet and a concise one-pager. High level answers below; we will attach the detailed matrix and a worked example in the next message.

High-level:
- Uptime tiers: 99.5 / 99.9 / 99.95 (measured monthly, wall-clock). Each tier has an associated credit slab that increases with lower achieved availability.
- Credits: Tiered percentage of monthly invoice applied as service credit (e.g., 99.9 -> 10% credit band; 99.5 -> higher). Credits are applied pro-rata for partial-month events.
- Response SLAs: P1 (severity: production outage impacting customers) — target response TTR: 1 hour (24x7 optional), P2 — 4 hours, P3 — next-business-day triage.
- Escalation: On-call -> senior on-call -> SEEM (service engineering engagement manager) -> director-level escalation windows (30 / 60 / 180 minutes). Exec escalation available for enterprise commitments.
- Differentiated business-hours pricing: Yes — we can offer business-hours-only (Mon–Fri, 9–5 local) with reduced pricing, or 24x7 premium with accelerated P1 targets.

I'll send the spreadsheet and a worked example in ~90 minutes. If you prefer a call to review the matrix, I can book 30 min tomorrow.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Support coverage slab structuring & volume incentive — detailed matrix + worked example

Tom / team —

Attached: coverage-slabs-v1.xlsx and example-pricing-calc.csv along with a short SLA-term-summary.pdf. Highlights from the workbook (quick digest):

1) Availability / credit bands (monthly measurement):
   - 99.95%+ : No credit (standard availability)
   - 99.9%–99.949% : 10% of monthly service fee credit
   - 99.5%–99.899% : 30% credit
   - <99.5% : 60% credit + dedicated remediation review

2) Response definitions (examples we propose):
   - P1 (Critical): Complete service/blocker — Response target 1 hour (24x7) or 2 hours (business-hours only); Escalation path: on-call -> senior -> SEEM -> Dir Ops (15/45/120 mins)
   - P2 (High): Major feature impacted — Response target 4 hours (business-hours)
   - P3 (Normal): Minor / advisory — Response target next-business-day

3) Volume incentive / discount scaffolding (illustrative):
   - Commit <$100k/year: standard list prices
   - Commit $100k–$249k/year: 7% volume discount; SLA credits as above
   - Commit $250k–$499k/year: 12% volume discount + 1% credit uplift (credits paid at +1% of monthly fee)
   - Commit >= $500k/year: 15% volume discount + 2% credit uplift + prioritized roadmap syncs

4) Dedicated capacity add-on: additional 8–12% off list for reserved GPU pools (depends on term & concurrency).

Worked example (from example-pricing-calc.csv) for $300k ARR:
   - Base list: $300,000
   - Volume discount (12%): -$36,000 -> $264,000 net
   - Credit uplift (1%): effectively increases potential monthly credit cap by ~$3,000/year in payout terms
   - Proposed pilot offer: 6-month managed commit with 99.9% SLA, 24x7 P1 at 1 hour — we can front-load a 10% onboarding credit for the first month to offset migration risk.

Notes & edge cases:
- Credit application is monthly and pro-rated for partial-month windows (yes, we prorate if an incident affects only a portion of the month).
- Credits are applied as invoice credits, not cash refunds (can be discussed for enterprise contracting).
- SLAs are measured on production/tiered services only (we exclude pre-prod/staging unless specifically included).

If this looks good, Marcus / Jordan — propose we offer the $300k ARR example as a 6-month pilot with the 12% volume discount and 1% credit uplift, then revisit at the 6-month milestone for potential uplift to the >=$500k slab.

— Kimberly
Director, Pricing & Solutions — Redwood Inference

Appreciate the detailed matrix — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from SRE and legal:

- Business-hours vs 24x7: Can you show incremental pricing difference for providing 24x7 P1 at 1 hour vs business-hours-only P1 at 2 hours? We need a clean delta number.
- Partial-month outages: Confirmed you prorate credits, but is the credit calculation based on calendar month or rolling 30-day window? Procurement prefers calendar month.
- We also want to confirm whether credits are the sole remedy or if BrightCart can request cash refunds for outages above the >60% band (we may escalate this to legal).

Would you also share a redline-ready offer we can circulate to legal? Attaching our SRE question list again. If possible, add a short note describing how executive escalation is triggered (who signs off).

If this looks matchable, we are prepared to move to a binding PO within two weeks.

Thanks — Tom

Tom —

Thanks — and great to hear you are ready to move. Below are direct answers plus a consolidated offer. We're attaching a redline-ready PDF (redwood-offer-BRG-4127.pdf).

Direct answers:
- 24x7 vs business-hours delta: For the 1-hour P1 target 24x7 we typically charge ~18% uplift over the business-hours-only pricing for the same commit and term. For $300k ARR illustrative: business-hours P1 (2 hr) net: $264k (after 12% discount); 24x7 P1 (1 hr) net: ~ $312k equivalent before re-applying volume bands (we modeled this in the attached pricing calc). Exact uplift depends on headcount and reserved capacity assumptions.
- Credit window: We use calendar-month measurement for availability and credits are calculated against that monthly invoice (this aligns with procurement preference).
- Credits vs cash: Standard is invoice credits. For enterprise commitments (>= $500k or negotiated PO language) we can discuss cash remedies; the redline contains optional language for a cash remedy clause for the <99.5 band to be reviewed by legal.
- Executive escalation: Triggered when a P1 is unresolved beyond the senior escalation window (per the matrix). The first exec notification is the Redwood Director of Ops; exec call within 60 minutes of that notification. Names and direct numbers are in the redline appendix.

Consolidated offer (proposed):
- Term: 6 months pilot (pre-paid) representing a $280,000 commit
- Coverage: 99.9% SLA (calendar-month measurement)
- Support: 24x7 P1 response target 1 hour, full escalation ladder
- Commercials: 15% volume discount on list (pilot price), plus 2% credit uplift (applied to monthly credit cap)
- Credits: monthly invoice credits, prorated to calendar month; optional cash remedy language for <99.5 band under enterprise review
- Onboarding: 10% onboarding credit in month 1

Next steps: I've attached the redline-ready PDF. If that aligns, Jordan will follow up to arrange a DocuSign envelope and a kick-off call. Link to book a quick review: https://cal.redwood.com/marcus/30min

Would you like us to include an explicit 24x7 delta line-item in the redline or keep it as an uplift percentage?

— Marcus
